Seminar Title:

Health, Functionality and Vulnerability in Later Life: A Multidimensional Approach to Healthy Ageing in India

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Humanities and Social Sciences

Speaker Name:

Kshirabdhi Tanaya Patra ( Rollno : 521hs2001)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

HS Seminar Room

Date and Time:

18 Nov 2026 12.15 PM

Contact:

Jalandhar Pradhan

Abstract:

Ageing is a multidimensional process that extends beyond the presence or absence of disease. It encompasses physical health, intrinsic capacity, functional ability and social well-being. In this context, healthy ageing and frailty represent an important and interconnected dimensions of later life. Their relationship is shaped by socioeconomic inequalities, financial security and the availability of care and support. However, the interplay among healthy ageing and frailty remains limited in the Indian context. Against this background, the present study aims to examine the interconnectedness of healthy ageing and frailty among older adults in India through four major objectives: first, assessing socioeconomic inequalities in healthy ageing secondly, examining the variation in healthy ageing across different levels of frailty among older adults in India.&nbsp thirdly, analysing the relationship between financial vulnerability and functional ability among older adults in India and fourth, exploring the role of functional limitation in care arrangements and dependency among older adults. The Present study uses data from Wave 1 of the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI), conducted during 2017-18. Appropriate econometric models are applied to examine the research objectives. The findings are expected to contribute to evidence-based policies and interventions that promote healthy ageing, reduce vulnerability and support functional independence and well-being in later life.
